I attached a small CSV snapshot (usage_snapshot_2028-01-08.csv) with the request ids and timestamps.

Quick questions: can you confirm whether those requests were billed as normal production tokens or if a different attribution (eg. staging vs prod) caused the multiplier? We were on a postpay plan so this spike is material for our month.

We'd appreciate a short note on root cause and whether a provisional credit is possible while we investigate on our side.

Hi all — quick summary from Billing & Metering after an initial pass.

What we found (short):
- The tokens in your snapshot were ingested and billed to your account entity for the UTC window 2028-01-08 23:38:00 -> 2028-01-09 01:22:00.
- The reason the counts look ~8x is that the job in question replayed the same payload with differing session_ids; our per-request attribution keys (request_id + session_id) treated them as unique and produced full token counts each run.
- Metering detail: we are using a rolling-window prefix attribution that looks at the session_id namespace for deduplication within a 10-minute window. Because the replay interval between bursts was ~12 minutes, deduplication did not trigger.

Evidence attached: ingest-log-snippet.txt (shows repeated request ids with incremented session_id suffixes) and a query extract we ran against the ledger.

Proposed remediation steps:
1) We can apply a provisional partial credit equal to the estimated duplicated-token portion while we complete a full forensic export.
2) We recommend configuring the replay job to preserve request_id and session_id across retries or set a shorter inter-burst spacing to fall within our 10-minute dedupe window.

Next actions for you: confirm whether the replay tool can keep a stable session_id or if you prefer us to proceed with the provisional credit request. If you approve the provisional credit we will issue a credit note and flag the invoice as pending until the full audit completes.

Let me know and I'll open BILL-872 for the audit and provisional credit.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Billing Operations — Redwood Inference
